modern: Mimes, war, astonishment, torpor, slavery will daily wipe out those holy principles of yours. How many things do you imagine without studying nature, and how many do you neglect? But it is your duty so to look at and so to do everything that at the same time the power of dealing with circumstances is perfected, and the contemplative faculty is exercised, and the confidence which comes from the knowledge of each single thing is maintained without being shown, but yet not concealed. For when will you enjoy simplicity, when seriousness, and when the knowledge of every single thing, both what it is in substance, and what place it has in the universe, and how long it is formed to exist, and what things it is made of, and to whom it can belong, and who are able both to give it and take it away?
original: Mimi, war, astonishment, torpor, slavery, will daily wipe out those holy principles of thine. How many things without studying nature dost thou imagine, and how many dost thou neglect? But it is thy duty so to look on and so to do everything, that at the same time the power of dealing with circumstances is perfected, and the contemplative faculty is exercised, and the confidence which comes from the knowledge of each several thing is maintained without showing it, but yet not concealed. explained.summary:
Ordinary life wears your principles away day by day: entertainment, conflict, panic, sluggishness, being at others’ beck and call. Marcus warns himself how much he takes for granted without thinking it through.

The remedy is to handle each task so that you get better at the practical side while still thinking clearly, with a quiet confidence that comes from understanding things, neither flaunted nor hidden. He wants to see each thing for what it is: what it’s made of, how long it lasts, where it fits, and who can give it or take it away.
explained.today: The modern list might be streaming shows, office politics, the news alert that makes your stomach drop, the mid-afternoon slump and an inbox that sets your agenda. Any of them can push your values out of mind before lunchtime.
